messages:
Anika: Heads up — onboarding atlas-40k (open). Found a reproducible token misalignment when running int4 quantized weights with longcontext >48k. Steps and a short log below.

Ravi: Can you paste the minimal repro command?

Anika: Sure — run on a single shard with priming + streaming generation:
```bash
python tools/long_fuzz.py --model atlas-40k-int4 --prefill-chunk 2048 --max-tokens 65536 --seed 42 --stream
```
Tail of the decoder diff at ~48256 tokens: `... token_48254 token_48255 -> token_48253 token_48254` (shift by -2).

Jo: I tried same inputs but with int8 and float16 — int8/float16 stable, only int4 shows the shift. Looks like a precision/rotation interaction rather than pure indexing bug.

perf-bot: benchmark/atlas-40k-int4-longctx-48k: alignment_shift > 0.8 tokens/sec at 48k, ppl delta +4.2 vs float16 (summary).

Ethan: My first guess: quantized trig table precision for RoPE/sincos is producing angle quantization noise that accumulates over long sequences. If sine/cos values are 8-bit-ish, repeated rotations amplify tiny errors. Try clamping rotary scaling or using a higher-resolution sin/cos table during inference.

Anika: Agreed. Planning a 3x test matrix: (A) int4 baseline, (B) int4 + high-res sincos table (float32 cache), (C) int4 + posscale clamp (0.125 / 0.5 / 1.0). Also cross-run with prefix-eviction enabled/disabled.

Jo: Can we also measure a simple "token alignment metric" — count of token index mismatches vs float16 baseline over sliding windows of 1024 tokens? That will be easier to aggregate than BLEU here.

Ravi: Queued runs on ded-dev-6 and ded-dev-7 (job ids 4821 / 4822). Will dump full kv-index checksums every 4096 tokens: `kv_dump --every 4096 --out /tmp/kv-dump-{{job}}.bin`.

Anika: Also adding a synthetic stress harness: `tools/longchain_fuzz.py --pattern rolling-prefix --window 65536 --chunk 1024 --iters 100`. This will help exercise prefill/eviction boundaries.

Ethan: If the sincos table fix helps, it's a cheap runtime change: load high-precision trig LUT into pinned memory and use fp32 for the rotate ops while keeping matmuls int4. If that fails, fallback ideas: 64-bit kv indices (unlikely), or runtime corrective scaling of RoPE angles during quantization.

Jo: I'm opening an eval PR with goldset-long-10k templates to compute perplexity + alignment-score + token-shift histogram. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/llm-evals/pull/214 (draft).

Anika: tagging @sofia for SLO/throughput implications — using fp32 sincos may bump token latency ~5-10% but could be tolerable for dedicated canary.

sofia: noted. If canary shows alignment restored with <10% perf impact, we can roll to a small % of dedicated capacity and run customer shadow traffic for 48h. Please include per-token latency breakdown in the run artifacts.

Ravi: Posted initial kv checksums and one failing trace: https://ci.redwood/atlas-onboard/4821/logs — see `trace_048256.txt` for token drift snapshot.

Anika: Perfect. We'll reconvene when the three test variations finish. If anyone finds a simpler repro or a deterministic min-case, drop it here (short is better). :thumbsup:

perf-bot: queued 6 jobs, ETA ~2h for first results.
